content.text: {"overall_verdict":"MEETS_WITH_LIMITED_GAPS","verdict_reason":"The chapter's integrated core survives the frozen rubric: it retains the received Masoretic readings as true, proposes consonantally identical second hearings that each pass the symmetrical admission gate on attested lexemes and productive grammar, honestly footnotes its weakest formation (the unattested Hithpael of the silence-root), and imports its symbolic identities from the independently frozen background packet rather than from the target passage. However, a small number of outcome-relevant gaps remain: the calendar-inversion claim (month beginning at the full moon versus the conjunction) rests on background material not established within the packet; Rule 4 stages 4 and 7 (strongest rival joint model and reversal conditions) are not executed for the eclipse synthesis; and the rubric supplies no rule for grading claims of intended polysemy ('spoken once, heard twice'), so the chapter's move from admissibility of the second hearings to their assertion as disclosed meaning cannot be adjudicated. These require narrowing or documentation, not reconstruction.","rule_audit":[{"rule":"1","result":"PASS","reason":"The chapter treats the Masoretic pointing as one reading-tradition witness without granting it a presumption or imposing an extra burden on it: it explicitly affirms 'the received reading is true' for eddammeh, retains 'north' for tsaphon ('the north reading remains true'), and retains 'throne' for kisse. No dependent witnesses are multiplied. One residual issue: the second hearings are asserted as co-intended rather than labeled with an underdetermination caveat, which is an analog of the labeling discipline Rule 1 requires when comparison does not select a winner."},{"rule":"2","result":"PASS","reason":"Strong's, Gesenius (with section numbers), and the ASV are cited for their data and arguments (attested spellings in Prov 7:20, Ps 81:3, Job 26:9; ל-marked objects in 2 Sam 3:30, Num 32:15, 1 Sam 23:10; Hithpael assimilation before ד), not for their status. No appeal to tradition, majority, or authority is used as proof of a reading. Minor caution: the Strong's etymology of kisse as 'covered seat' is an etymological datum given interpretive weight, but it is supporting color, not the load-bearing proof."},{"rule":"3","result":"PARTIAL","reason":"Each proposed alternate accounts for the same consonants (שחר, צפון, כסא, אדמה), uses independently attested lexemes (shachar 'be black' in Job 30:30; tsafun in Ezek 7:22/Ps 83:3; keseh in Prov 7:20/Ps 81:3; damah III in Isa 15:1/Hos 4:5), is morphologically possible, and yields a coherent clause; the Masoretic candidates pass the same gate and are retained. The footnote conceding no second Hithpael of the silence-root and reliance on productive formation is exactly the disclosure Rule 3 demands. PARTIAL because the chapter's rhetoric ('the words have earned their readings') advances beyond admissibility toward asserted intent without the comparative stage that would justify it, and the suffixed keseh form ('my full-moon seat') is regular but unattested and should be flagged as such."},{"rule":"4","result":"PARTIAL","reason":"Stages 1-3 are respected: the celestial symbol system is frozen in the prior chapter without using Isaiah 14, both candidates pass Rule 3, and the background genuinely makes the boast's cluster (stars, throne, appointed assembly, hidden recess, dark cloud, Highest) more expected under the eclipse synthesis, unifying otherwise independent details including the yarkete reversal in v.15 and Daniel 7:25. Stages 4 and 7 are not executed: the chapter never constructs the strongest rival joint model (royal-hubris/Zion reading in which tsaphon is the fixed Ps 48:2 idiom and the boast is spatial arrogation of God's mountain with no eclipse), and states no reversal conditions. Stage 6 dependency risk: the kisse/keseh identity is used in the background chapter (Ps 89) and again here; the lexical fact is independently attested so it is shared vocabulary rather than strict double counting, but the identity inference must be counted once. The calendar sub-claim additionally leans on a background assertion (full-moon month start) not established by frozen evidence."}],"claim_ledger":[{"claim":"Helel ben shachar can be heard both as 'son of dawn' and, by same-consonant wordplay, as 'son/bearer of blackness' (verb shachar, Job 30:30).","category":"LINGUISTIC_VOCALIZATION","book_candidate":"shachar heard against the verb-root 'be black' as a characterizing wordplay","strongest_rival":"MT noun shachar 'dawn' as the sole sense ('son of the morning/dawn')","book_admission":"PASS","rival_admission":"PASS","comparison":"RIVAL_BETTER_SUPPORTED","evidence_origins":["TARGET_CHAPTER","EVALUATOR_KNOWLEDGE"],"reason":"The verb is attested (Job 30:30) and the consonants are identical, so the wordplay is admissible; the chapter's own footnote correctly labels it wordplay and concedes the noun 'dawn' is grammatically primary. The construct ben + noun favors 'dawn' as the primary hearing; 'son of blackness' as a noun sense would need a different nominal form (shechor/shacharut). Evaluator lexical knowledge requires source verification.","gap_owner":"NONE","outcome_changing_evidence":"Attestation of the bare noun shachar meaning 'blackness' would raise the alternate from wordplay to a full lexical rival; conversely, evidence that the verb root is a homonym confined to skin-discoloration contexts would weaken the characterization."},{"claim":"Har moed carries moed's full lexical field — appointed time, place, and meeting — so the phrase names the mountain of the appointed assembly.","category":"LEXICAL_OR_GRAMMATICAL","book_candidate":"moed with its full attested field (Lev 23:2 moedim as proclaimed holy convocations)","strongest_rival":"moed narrowly as 'assembly/council' (the divine-council mount)","book_admission":"PASS","rival_admission":"PASS","comparison":"UNDERDETERMINED","evidence_origins":["TARGET_CHAPTER","EVALUATOR_KNOWLEDGE"],"reason":"Both senses are within the attested field; Leviticus 23:2 genuinely binds appointed times to proclaimed assemblies. Neither hearing excludes the other, and the chapter does not need the narrower rival to fail. The choice between them is a downstream synthesis question, not decidable at the lexical gate.","gap_owner":"NONE","outcome_changing_evidence":"A demonstration that har moed is a fixed idiom in cognate or biblical usage restricted to the council sense would narrow the field; conversely, other biblical collocations of moed + place-of-worship vocabulary would strengthen the fuller field."},{"claim":"Yarkete tsaphon can be heard as 'recesses of the north' (retained, with Ps 48:2 tying it to Zion) and as 'innermost recesses of the hidden place' (tsafun).","category":"LINGUISTIC_VOCALIZATION","book_candidate":"tsafun 'hidden/treasured' (Ezek 7:22; Ps 83:3) as a second hearing of צפון","strongest_rival":"MT tsaphon 'north' as a fixed idiom (Ps 48:2 yarkete tsaphon of Zion)","book_admission":"PASS","rival_admission":"PASS","comparison":"RIVAL_BETTER_SUPPORTED","evidence_origins":["TARGET_CHAPTER","EVALUATOR_KNOWLEDGE"],"reason":"The consonants are identical and the passive participle tsafun is independently attested in exactly the senses claimed. The chapter retains the north reading and even supplies the rival's best evidence (Ps 48:2) itself — commendable symmetry. The fixed-idiom parallel makes 'north' the better-supported primary hearing; the hidden-place hearing is an admissible overlay whose intentionality is not adjudicable under the rubric.","gap_owner":"PROTOCOL_MISSING_RULE","outcome_changing_evidence":"Another biblical yarkete + tsafun collocation demonstrably meaning 'hidden recesses' would upgrade the alternate; a rule for grading intended polysemy would allow the dual hearing itself to be scored."},{"claim":"The consonants of 'my throne' (כסא + suffix) can also be heard as 'my full-moon seat' (keseh), since throne and full moon share both biblical spellings (כסא Prov 7:20; כסה Ps 81:3; Job 26:9 for the throne side).","category":"LINGUISTIC_VOCALIZATION","book_candidate":"keseh 'full moon' as a second hearing of the suffixed noun","strongest_rival":"MT kisse' 'throne' as the sole sense","book_admission":"PASS","rival_admission":"PASS","comparison":"RIVAL_BETTER_SUPPORTED","evidence_origins":["TARGET_CHAPTER","BACKGROUND_PACKET","EVALUATOR_KNOWLEDGE"],"reason":"The spelling facts cited are correct and independently attested; the Job 26:9 ambiguity is real and quoted. 'Throne' remains the better-supported primary sense in a boast about a seat of rule, and a suffixed keseh is regular but unattested — a fact the chapter should state. Ps 89:36-37 (also in the frozen background) legitimately joins throne and moon imagery before the wordplay is asked to carry weight, but that identity inference may be counted only once across background and target.","gap_owner":"CHAPTER_MISSING_EVIDENCE","outcome_changing_evidence":"A footnote conceding the unattested suffixed keseh form; any attested suffixed or construct use of keseh would materially strengthen the hearing, and evidence that keseh is a loanword with a distinct consonantal history would weaken it."},{"claim":"Eddammeh le-elyon is 'spoken once, heard twice': 'I will make myself like the Most High' (retained) and 'I will bring the Highest to silence for myself' (damah III, Hithpael for-oneself, ל-marked object).","category":"LINGUISTIC_VOCALIZATION","book_candidate":"Hithpael of damah III 'cease/destroy' with external ל-marked object","strongest_rival":"MT Hithpael of damah I 'be like' with ל marking the standard of comparison","book_admission":"PASS","rival_admission":"PASS","comparison":"RIVAL_BETTER_SUPPORTED","evidence_origins":["TARGET_CHAPTER","EVALUATOR_KNOWLEDGE"],"reason":"The alternate stacks individually attested features (damah III in Isa 15:1/Hos 4:5; ת-assimilation before ד; Hithpael benefactive nuance; ל-marked objects per 2 Sam 3:30 etc.) into a jointly unattested construction, which the footnote candidly discloses; under Rule 3 this is admissible via productive rules. The rival is the far better-supported construction: damah + ל comparison is common and contextually natural after a chain of self-exalting verbs. The chapter correctly does not claim the alternate defeats the received reading; its claim of co-intent is what the rubric cannot score.","gap_owner":"PROTOCOL_MISSING_RULE","outcome_changing_evidence":"Any attested transitive Hithpael of a damah-type root, or a second biblical locus pairing the silence-root with elyon/light vocabulary, would raise the alternate's weight; demonstration that Hithpael + ל-object is unattested for stative-derived roots would push it to FAIL."},{"claim":"The imported symbol identities — stars = the righteous (Dan 12:3), mountain = kingdom (Dan 2), moon appointed for moedim (Ps 104:19), full moon = the Son's faithful-witness throne (Ps 89:36-37) — govern the boast's imagery.","category":"BACKGROUND_HYPOTHESIS","book_candidate":"The frozen celestial symbol system of the prior chapter","strongest_rival":"A non-personal astral reading in which the lights are only calendar markers and the boast's imagery is conventional royal hyperbole","book_admission":"PASS","rival_admission":"PASS","comparison":"NOT_COMPARATIVE","evidence_origins":["BACKGROUND_PACKET"],"reason":"By experiment design the symbol system is independently frozen and was established without Isaiah 14; the target chapter correctly defers the symbols until after the words are gated ('only after the words stand do the symbols enter'). Its application here is legitimate importation, not fresh proof. The rival is not defeated within the packet, but the packet's premises authorize the symbolic method.","gap_owner":"NONE","outcome_changing_evidence":"Evidence that the background chapter's key identifications themselves depended on Isaiah 14 would create circularity; none is present in the packet."},{"claim":"The counterfeit seat is 'covered in darkness' — derived from the blackness wordplay, the hidden recess, and the dark-cloud high place — the inverse of the light-covered legitimate throne (Ps 104:2).","category":"SYMBOLIC_DERIVATION","book_candidate":"Darkness-covered lunar seat as the composite of the gated word-level hearings","strongest_rival":"The images read severally: cloud-heights as royal hubris, north as Zion, with no lunar covering","book_admission":"PASS","rival_admission":"PASS","comparison":"UNDERDETERMINED","evidence_origins":["TARGET_CHAPTER","BACKGROUND_PACKET"],"reason":"The derivation is internally coherent and correctly built only from elements that individually passed the gate; av 'dark cloud-mass' is standard lexicon. But the composite inherits the probability of its weakest members (the keseh and blackness hearings), and the rival severally-read model explains the same words with fewer stacked hearings. Neither joint model is compared in the chapter.","gap_owner":"CHAPTER_MISSING_EVIDENCE","outcome_changing_evidence":"Execution of the Rule 4 stage-4 comparison; independent biblical linkage of covering-vocabulary with the darkened moon would strengthen the composite."},{"claim":"Astronomical mechanics: the full moon stands opposite the sun and can never cover it; only the moon at conjunction can enter the sun's apparent place and cover it, becoming 'like' the sun by taking its visible position while depending on the light it covers.","category":"HISTORICAL_OR_ASTRONOMICAL","book_candidate":"Solar-eclipse geometry as the physical performance of the boast","strongest_rival":"No celestial event intended; the boast is purely spatial-political hyperbole","book_admission":"PASS","rival_admission":"PASS","comparison":"UNDERDETERMINED","evidence_origins":["TARGET_CHAPTER","EVALUATOR_KNOWLEDGE"],"reason":"The astronomy stated is uncontroversially correct (evaluator knowledge, requiring no source beyond basic celestial mechanics). Whether Isaiah 14 encodes it is the consilience question: the eclipse model genuinely unifies stars, seat, hiddenness, cloud, likeness-by-position, and silencing, but this is accommodation after seeing the text, which Rule 4 says carries limited weight absent the rival-joint-model comparison the chapter omits.","gap_owner":"CHAPTER_MISSING_EVIDENCE","outcome_changing_evidence":"A stage-4/stage-7 analysis; any prior-scripture text independently associating eclipse phenomena with usurpation language would convert accommodation into comparative expectedness."},{"claim":"Reciprocal consilience: the frozen symbol system plus the second hearings jointly explain the boast's 'strange precision' better than the abstract-ambition reading, and Isaiah 14 reciprocally strengthens the symbol system.","category":"RECIPROCAL_CONSILIENCE","book_candidate":"Joint model: celestial household symbols + covered-lunar-seat hearings of Isaiah 14","strongest_rival":"Joint model: canonical Zion-hubris reading (Ps 48:2 idiom, spatial arrogation of God's mount) + Daniel 7:25 read independently","book_admission":"PASS","rival_admission":"PASS","comparison":"UNDERDETERMINED","evidence_origins":["TARGET_CHAPTER","BACKGROUND_PACKET"],"reason":"The background was frozen without the target (stage 1 satisfied) and the target supplies incremental unification (the yarkete reversal in v.15, the moed/assembly link, the Daniel 7:25 convergence). But the chapter never states the rival joint model's explanatory ledger or its own reversal conditions, and the kisse/keseh identity inference is reused from the background and must be counted once. Under Rule 4 the support is real but incompletely demonstrated.","gap_owner":"CHAPTER_MISSING_EVIDENCE","outcome_changing_evidence":"A compact rival-model comparison; if the rival explains all material facts with fewer unsupported assumptions, the consilience claim reverses."},{"claim":"Calendar corruption: the counterfeit claims the full-moon throne while moving the month's beginning to the hidden conjunction — the phase that can cover the sun — and Daniel 7:25 names this agenda.","category":"HISTORICAL_OR_ASTRONOMICAL","book_candidate":"Original month reckoned from the full moon; conjunction reckoning is the corruption","strongest_rival":"Month originally reckoned from the new moon/conjunction or first crescent (chodesh at month's head, keseh feast mid-month, cf. the chapter's own Ps 81:3 citation)","book_admission":"UNDERDETERMINED","rival_admission":"PASS","comparison":"RIVAL_BETTER_SUPPORTED","evidence_origins":["BACKGROUND_PACKET","EVALUATOR_KNOWLEDGE"],"reason":"The full-moon month-start hypothesis is asserted in the background chapter but rests there chiefly on a Rev 12:1 rendering from the Cochin Hebrew tradition (c. 1700), whose lineage, independence, and direction of translation are not evaluated as premise 7 requires; it is therefore not an 'independently established' background under Rule 4 stage 1. The chapter's own Ps 81:3 quotation (trumpet at chodesh... at keseh for the feast) is naturally read by the rival as new-moon month-head with full-moon feast. Evaluator historical knowledge (uniform ancient new-moon reckoning) requires source verification and is marked as such.","gap_owner":"CHAPTER_MISSING_EVIDENCE","outcome_changing_evidence":"Independent, lineage-evaluated evidence for full-moon month reckoning (e.g., a demonstrated pre-exilic usage of chodesh compatible with a full-moon head, or authentication of the Hebrew Revelation as an independent witness) would flip this to admissible; absent it, the sentence should be narrowed to a labeled hypothesis."},{"claim":"Amos 8:9-10 binds a noon sun-failure to an appointed feast and the mourning of an only son; the crucifixion darkness (Matt 27:45; Luke 23:44-45) is its canonical confirmation, turning the counterfeit's image into testimony.","category":"THEOLOGICAL_SYNTHESIS","book_candidate":"NT confirmation of a prophetic sign-pattern per premise 8 step 3","strongest_rival":"Amos 8 as judgment imagery on Israel's eighth-century feasts with no crucifixion referent","book_admission":"PASS","rival_admission":"PASS","comparison":"UNDERDETERMINED","evidence_origins":["TARGET_CHAPTER"],"reason":"The synthesis uses the NT exactly as premise 8 permits — as confirmation after OT derivation — and the chapter properly refuses the natural-eclipse reduction (Passover falls at full moon; the duration exceeds totality), using the eclipse's 'exact act' typologically rather than astronomically. The correspondence (noon darkness, feast, only-son mourning) is textually real; whether Amos predicts the cross or the cross echoes Amos is a fulfillment-identification the packet permits but does not force.","gap_owner":"NONE","outcome_changing_evidence":"None needed for admissibility; a demonstration that Amos 8's 'only son' idiom is a fixed mourning simile with no referential force would reduce the confirmation's weight."},{"claim":"The boast is Satan's plan ('Lucifer's Declared Plan'), read through and beyond the king of Babylon, with 2 Cor 11:14 explaining the bright-appearance/darkness-production mechanism.","category":"THEOLOGICAL_SYNTHESIS","book_candidate":"Dual reference: the mashal against Babylon's king discloses the rebel power behind him","strongest_rival":"The taunt addresses only the human king of Babylon (Isa 14:4, quoted by the chapter itself)","book_admission":"PASS","rival_admission":"PASS","comparison":"UNDERDETERMINED","evidence_origins":["TARGET_CHAPTER","EVALUATOR_KNOWLEDGE"],"reason":"The chapter presumes rather than argues the identification; it cites Isa 14:4 (which names the king of Babylon) and Amos 4:13 for the heart-reading frame, then applies 2 Cor 11:14 as NT confirmation. Under the canon premises a dual-reference synthesis is permissible, but the bridging step from king to rebel power is asserted, not derived. The core word-level and symbol-level analysis survives under either referent, so the gap is limited rather than structural.","gap_owner":"CHAPTER_MISSING_EVIDENCE","outcome_changing_evidence":"One bridging sentence or footnote deriving the dual reference from prior scripture (e.g., the pattern of addressing the power behind a throne) would close the gap; a rule for grading typological referent-identification would also resolve it."}],"reciprocal_consilience":{"verdict":"VALID_BUT_INCOMPLETE","independent_background_support":"The celestial symbol system (sun=Father via Ps 84:11; moon=Son/faithful witness via Ps 89:36-37 and Rev 1:5; stars=righteous via Dan 12:3; moon appointed for moedim via Ps 104:19; kisse/keseh spelling facts via Prov 7:20 and Ps 81:3) is frozen in the prior chapter without any use of Isaiah 14. Its core identifications rest on canonical texts, though one sub-hypothesis inside it — the full-moon head of the month/year — rests on a late Hebrew Revelation rendering whose witness value is not established in the packet.","incremental_target_evidence":"Isaiah 14 contributes genuinely new unification: the yarkete recess/pit reversal in v.15 answering the boast in its own word; the har moed link joining the seat to the appointed assembly; the dark-cloud and hiddenness vocabulary matching the covered-conjunction geometry; and the convergence with Daniel 7:25's times-and-laws agenda. None of these facts was used to establish the background system.","dependency_or_duplication_risk":"The kisse=keseh identity inference appears in both the background chapter (Ps 89 discussion) and the target (Isa 14:13); the underlying spelling attestations are independent canonical facts, but the identity inference must be counted once, not twice. The 'moon marks the moedim' premise is likewise shared and correctly used as background rather than re-proved. The calendar-inversion sub-claim, however, reuses the background's weakest assertion (full-moon month start) as if established.","strongest_rival_joint_model":"The canonical royal-hubris model: yarkete tsaphon as the fixed Ps 48:2 idiom for Zion; the boast as spatial arrogation of God's own mountain and council above the stars; eddammeh le-elyon as the well-attested comparison construction; Daniel 7:25 read as the persecuting power's assault on covenant observance without any eclipse figure. This model explains the same consonantal text with fewer stacked hearings and no unattested constructions, but it leaves the specific clustering of seat, hiddenness, dark cloud, appointed assembly, and the light-silencing effect as unconnected images.","comparative_result":"The book's joint model unifies more independent details; the rival requires fewer assumptions. Because the chapter never lays the two ledgers side by side or states reversal conditions (Rule 4 stages 4 and 7), the comparison remains formally incomplete: the consilience is real but not demonstrated to the r
